decks.module: Who needs a license and license classes

cards.front: Who may drive legally in New York, and what must new permanent residents do with an old license?
cards.back: Legal driving here needs a valid license, a current out-of-state or foreign license is honored, nobody under sixteen may drive, new permanent residents trade in the old license within thirty days, holding two state licenses at once is generally unlawful.

cards.front: What happens to someone who forges or alters a motor-vehicle document?
cards.back: Forging or altering any motor-vehicle document is a crime risking suspension or revocation plus prosecution toward a fine or jail.

cards.front: Which vehicles and loads require a commercial license?
cards.back: Commercial licenses cover rigs rated over twenty-six thousand pounds, heavy combinations towing over ten thousand, vehicles for fifteen or more besides the driver, Article nineteen-A buses, and placarded hazmat loads.

cards.front: Who may get a Class D license, and what may it drive?
cards.back: Class D starts at eighteen, or seventeen with driver education, for vehicles to twenty-six thousand pounds, towing to ten thousand or more while the combination stays within twenty-six thousand, plus Class B and C mopeds.

cards.front: What two kinds of triggers make a license commercial?
cards.back: Commercial duty turns on either size or service: twenty-six thousand pounds of rating, fifteen-plus carried people, Article nineteen-A bus status, or placarded hazmat, while ordinary cars and small trailers stay non-commercial.

cards.front: How do Class DJ and Class E differ from Class D?
cards.back: Class DJ starts at sixteen with lower weight and tow caps under junior limits; Class E starts at eighteen, matches Class D, and adds paid carriage to fourteen passengers except Article nineteen-A buses.

cards.front: How do Class D, Class DJ and Class E differ by age and purpose?
cards.back: Class D is the adult operator license from eighteen, Class DJ the junior version from sixteen with lower caps, and Class E the hire-carrying counterpart of D from eighteen, so age plus purpose separates all three.

cards.front: Who may get Class M and Class MJ licenses, and how is a second class shown?
cards.back: Class M starts at eighteen, or seventeen with driver education, and Class MJ at sixteen, both for motorcycles and mopeds with junior limits on MJ; holding motorcycle plus another class prints both on one card such as Class DM.

decks.module: Enhanced, REAL ID and the R endorsement

cards.front: What can the Enhanced license be used for, and who may get one?
cards.back: The Enhanced license serves land and sea crossings with Canada, Mexico, Bermuda and the Caribbean as a passport substitute, works for domestic air travel, needs state residence plus United States citizenship, and also issues for commercial and motorcycle classes.

cards.front: What is REAL ID, and what do domestic flyers show?
cards.back: REAL ID is the federal standard born of the nine over eleven Commission for state cards used at federal checkpoints, so domestic flyers show a REAL ID, an Enhanced license, or other federally accepted identification, obtained only at a motor-vehicle office.

cards.front: How does the Enhanced license differ from REAL ID?
cards.back: The Enhanced license proves citizenship for border crossings and domestic flights, while REAL ID only certifies the card meets federal checkpoint standards, so crossing needs the former and flying accepts either.

cards.front: Since when do domestic flights need REAL ID or similar, and what happens if you skip REAL ID?
cards.back: Since May three, two thousand twenty-three, domestic flights and secure federal sites need REAL ID, Enhanced, passport or accepted identification; REAL ID issues only in offices from October thirty, two thousand seventeen against original identity, Social Security, birth-date, status and dual residence proofs plus a photo, while skipping it keeps mail or web renewal with post-two thousand seventeen cards marked not for federal purposes and an eye test within six months, one year on clinical call, on form MV-six hundred nineteen.

cards.front: When is the R endorsement needed, and how is it earned?
cards.back: The R endorsement for personal-use rental or recreational rigs hauling household goods starts past twenty-six thousand pounds or forty feet for Class D and E drivers, needs form MV-forty-four and a permit fee covering at most two road tests, a road test in matching size and type with no written test beside a supervisor twenty-one or older licensed for the rig, about fifteen minutes of turns, intersections and curb backing, then an office visit and fee.

cards.front: What two triggers bring the R endorsement, and how does its test differ?
cards.back: The R endorsement trips on either bulk or length, past twenty-six thousand pounds or forty feet, and its road test has no written companion, unlike the ordinary license path.

cards.front: What steps does a first-time applicant take?
cards.back: First-timers file form MV-forty-four at any office or from the DMV website, pass vision and knowledge tests plus fees, and mostly finish a five-hour pre-licensing course and road test; the first license runs at most five years to the birth month and day with Class D, DJ, M and MJ fees set by age and birth date.

cards.front: What identity proofs must an applicant supply, and how many points must name proofs total?
cards.back: Applicants supply a Social Security number plus English name and age proofs from the point lists on forms MV-forty-four point one, MV-forty-four.1RID, ID-forty-four and ID-44RID; name proofs must total six points with one signed, and a current New York photo card alone is worth six points unless expired over two years.

cards.front: How does the application form relate to the six-point identity tally?
cards.back: Form MV-forty-four opens the application, but the six-point identity tally with one signed paper is a separate gate, and a current New York photo card alone clears all six points.

cards.front: Which documents are worth four points as proof of identity?
cards.back: Four-point proofs are DMV statements MV-forty-five for applicants under twenty-one, MV-45A for government-represented applicants, and MV-45B for homeless youth unusable for Enhanced or REAL ID; a valid United States passport or card; an English foreign passport with visa and entry proof or embassy-certified translation; a consular identity document; a photo foreign license; and a photo card from another United States jurisdiction or Canadian province, current or expired at most two years.

cards.front: Which documents are worth three points as proof of identity?
cards.back: Three-point papers are a valid re-entry permit, refugee travel document, citizenship or naturalization certificate, unexpired resident card, valid photo work-authorization card, military photo card for active, reserve or retired members, photo benefit card, and border-crossing card.

cards.front: Which documents are on the first list of two-point proofs?
cards.back: Two-point papers include a military dependent card, non-photo interim license or computer permit, title, registration, Social Security card, high-school photo ID with report card or transcript, and college photo ID with transcript.

cards.front: Which documents are on the second list of two-point proofs?
cards.back: More two-point papers are a government marriage, divorce or name-change record, professional license, pistol permit, tribal photo card, foreign-government marriage, divorce or name-change record, benefit card without photo, foreign school record with photo, and resident or work-authorization cards expired at most two years.

cards.front: Which documents are on the first list of one-point proofs?
cards.back: One-point papers are a major credit card, ATM card with preprinted name and signature, canceled check with preprinted name, bank record, employee ID, pay stub showing the name, check-cashing card with preprinted name and signature, life policy in force two years, health or prescription card, utility bill with name and address, diploma or equivalency, and a W-two showing the Social Security number.

cards.front: What finishes the one-point list, and which documents prove age?
cards.back: The list ends with a union card, veteran access photo card, court document naming the applicant, foreign school record without photo, municipal photo ID, tax transcript or taxpayer-number letter, and Social Security statement; age is proved by one government birth certificate, state or city birth-registration certificate, military photo ID, United States passport, foreign passport with immigration papers, or citizenship or naturalization certificate.

decks.module: Vision, written test and the permit

cards.front: What vision standard must applicants meet?
cards.back: Vision needs twenty-forty in at least one eye with or without correction, and failures or special lenses go to a DMV call center.

cards.front: What does the written test cover, and what does it take to pass?
cards.back: The Class D, M, DJ, MJ and E written test spans road rules, safe driving, signs, and alcohol and drug law, passing at fourteen of twenty including two of four sign items, with the manual's items and website quizzes as practice.

cards.front: Why can strong road-rules knowledge still fail the written test?
cards.back: The written test has twin bars, fourteen of twenty overall and two of four signs, so strong rules knowledge still fails without the sign minimum.

cards.front: What other manuals, languages and school pre-tests are available?
cards.back: Motorcycle applicants also study manual MV-21MC and commercial applicants manual CDL-ten for a separate test; Class D tests run multilingual on touch screens or paper; students from fifteen years eleven months may pre-test through OKTA at participating high schools in English or Spanish with instant on-screen scoring, and schools need no driver-ed program, just a connected computer, printer and monitor.

cards.front: How do vision screening, the written test and the school pre-test relate?
cards.back: Vision screening at twenty-forty and the written test are independent gates, and the OKTA online pre-test only works for students from fifteen years eleven months at participating schools.

cards.front: What does a student do after passing the online pre-test?
cards.back: Online passers take a receipt, instructions and forms to any office from age sixteen to apply, and failures retake online as often as the school allows.

cards.front: What do properly licensed, guardian, in loco parentis and school course mean?
cards.back: Properly licensed means licensed in-state for the driven vehicle; a guardian is a court-appointed durable stand-in parent; in loco parentis is a consented parent-role stand-in; a school course is state-approved instruction or Armed Forces training excluding zero-credit activities.

cards.front: What are the junior-permit day and night rules in the city and on Long Island?
cards.back: Junior-permit days run five morning to nine evening under a parent, guardian, in-loco-parentis adult, teacher or instructor with dual-control brakes in the city, the same list or a written designee on Long Island, while both regions ban night driving outright.

cards.front: What are the junior-permit day and night rules upstate?
cards.back: Upstate junior-permit days accept any supervisor twenty-one or older with a valid license, and upstate nights return to the five-person supervisor list.

cards.front: How do junior-permit night rules differ between downstate and upstate?
cards.back: Junior-permit nights ban city and Long Island driving outright yet allow supervised upstate driving, while days everywhere demand a qualified supervisor, tighter in the city and on Long Island than upstate.

cards.front: What counts as employment, work-study, medical and daycare trips, and which roads are off limits to permit holders?
cards.back: Employment is scheduled paid work excluding driving as the job, work-study is an approved program such as credit-bearing BOCES courses, medical trips cover needed household care, and daycare trips enable family work or study; permit holders always carry a twenty-one-or-older supervisor licensed for the vehicle, a parent, guardian or instructor in the city and on Long Island, and avoid test areas, city park streets, Triborough crossings, and the Cross County, Hutchinson River, Saw Mill River and Taconic parkways.

cards.front: How do supervisor requirements differ between the city, Long Island and upstate?
cards.back: The supervisor must be twenty-one or older and licensed for the vehicle everywhere, but the city and Long Island further require a parent, guardian or instructor, unlike upstate.

cards.front: What passenger and seating limits apply to junior-permit drivers?
cards.back: Junior-permit drivers take at most one under-twenty-one passenger unless immediate family or a qualifying supervisor rides along, belt every occupant with child restraints, seat only the supervisor up front, and face added junior sanctions in the next chapter.

decks.module: Preparing for and taking the road test

cards.front: How much practice is recommended before the road test, and what course must be finished?
cards.back: Test candidates should log fifty hours with fifteen after sunset and ten in heavier traffic, rehearse expressways beyond city streets, prefer school-based lessons, and finish an approved safe-driving course, automatic in driver education or as pre-licensing with an adult online pilot, before booking.

cards.front: What must in-person course graduates present at booking, and which course does not count?
cards.back: In-person course graduates present the certificate, valid one year, at booking, and the point-and-insurance crash-prevention course does not satisfy the requirement.

cards.front: What does the point-and-insurance crash-prevention course do?
cards.back: The certified crash-prevention course, sold privately in class or online as point-and-insurance reduction, erases up to four points when eligible, repeats every eighteen months, and cuts liability and collision base rates ten percent for three years.

cards.front: Can the point-and-insurance course replace the required safe-driving course?
cards.back: The DMV-certified Point and Insurance Reduction Program can reduce eligible driving-record points and lower base liability and collision insurance rates, but it does not satisfy the Safe Driving Course requirement.

cards.front: What does point relief give, and how is it related to test eligibility?
cards.back: When eligible, the Point and Insurance Reduction Program reduces up to four points from your driving record every eighteen months and qualifies you for at least a ten percent reduction in base liability and collision insurance premiums for three years, without meeting the Safe Driving Course requirement.

cards.front: How do juniors upgrade their license, and what papers are needed on test day?
cards.back: Juniors upgrade by filing the MV-two hundred eighty-five student certificate and surrendering the junior license, or hand the permit to the examiner for automatic upgrade, else limits run to eighteen; the permit must hold valid six months first, and test day needs MV-two hundred seventy-eight or MV-two hundred eighty-five on file, the photo permit, and a parental MV-two hundred sixty-two certifying fifty hours with fifteen after sunset.

cards.front: Which practice targets are recommendations, and which permit rule is a hard requirement?
cards.back: Before the road test, DMV states you should have at least fifty hours of practice—including at least fifteen after sunset and a recommended ten in moderate to heavy traffic—whereas a junior learner permit must be held in valid status for at least six months before taking the road test.

cards.front: What must the test car and the arriving driver bring, and how do you book?
cards.back: Test cars must be registered, inspected, insured, equipped and roadworthy with a clean free examiner belt, arriving drivers bring a twenty-one-or-older licensed supervisor, and motorcycle applicants supply a car, truck and driver for the examiner; other permit holders show photo permit plus MV-two hundred seventy-eight or MV-two hundred eighty-five on file, booking online or at one-five hundred eighteen-four hundred two-two thousand one hundred.

cards.front: What does each of the three test-day forms prove?
cards.back: MV-two hundred seventy-eight proves the five-hour course, MV-two hundred eighty-five proves student driver education, and MV-two hundred sixty-two certifies supervised hours, three papers with three distinct jobs at test time.

cards.front: What happens on and after road test day?
cards.back: Schedulers keep the MV-two hundred seventy-eight or MV-two hundred eighty-five proof ready, weather can cancel tests with online notices, and after the drive the examiner explains result delivery while an online interim license carried beside the permit covers driving until the photo card mails in about two weeks.

cards.front: What passenger and regional limits apply to junior-license holders?
cards.back: Junior-license holders take at most one non-family under-twenty-one passenger, belt all occupants with child restraints, face added sanctions in the next chapter, and follow Class DJ regional place, time and company limits.

cards.front: What proof do junior drivers need for solo job or school runs?
cards.back: Solo Nassau and Suffolk job runs, farm work included, need MV-58A employment proof, or upstate a dated signed employer letter naming business, driver, duties, schedule and a verification contact; solo school or work-study runs need a dated signed letterhead enrollment letter with official contact, activity schedule and places, and driver identity.

cards.front: How does the purpose of a solo junior run decide which proof is needed?
cards.back: Solo job runs need MV-58A employment proof, or upstate an employer letter, while solo school runs need a letterhead enrollment letter, so the destination picks the paper.

cards.front: What are the junior-license day and night limits in each region?
cards.back: Licensed-junior days allow city solo runs only straight between home and job, work-study, college, evening high school, driver education or farm work, or accompanied by a qualifying adult, with free daytime driving on Long Island and upstate; nights ban city driving, limit Long Island solos to school and farm shuttles, and limit upstate solos to job or school runs with other night driving adult-accompanied.

cards.front: How do junior-license night rules differ by region?
cards.back: Licensed-junior nights ban the city, shuttle school and farm trips on Long Island, and allow job or school runs upstate, a three-way split that mirrors but never matches the permit chart.

cards.front: What passenger and supervision rules apply to permit and junior motorcycle and moped riders?
cards.back: Permit and junior motorcycle and moped riders carry no passenger but the supervisor, who holds the same-class license, stays within a quarter mile in general control, and should keep the rider visible.

cards.front: What passenger and supervision rules apply to a Class M or MJ motorcycle or moped learner permit or junior license?
cards.back: A Class M or MJ motorcycle or moped learner permit or junior license allows no passenger except a supervising driver licensed for the same class, who must maintain general supervision and control within one quarter mile and should ideally keep the rider in sight.

cards.front: Where do New York junior credentials work, and how do you report address changes and renew?
cards.back: New York permits and junior licenses work elsewhere only where allowed under local limits, so visitors check with local authorities; address changes reach the DMV within ten days by mail, form MV-two hundred thirty-two or web with the new address inked on the license back; drivers track expiry, notices mail forty-five days ahead, missing notices mean an office visit, and renewal runs one year early.

cards.front: How long do service members keep their license, and when must out-of-state drivers apply?
cards.back: Service members keep their license through active duty plus six months after discharge on sixty-day MV-seventy-five notice; out-of-state and foreign licensees drive until residence, then apply within thirty days.

cards.front: What must new residents from other states, Canada or other countries do?
cards.back: New residents surrender United States or Canadian licenses with added identity proof plus vision, adding written, road and course work for short-held or long-expired licenses; other-country newcomers pass vision, course, surrender, written and road steps with the foreign card destroyed unless a written hold is filed and returned only after surrendering the New York card; young visitors obey both states' limits and nobody under sixteen drives.

cards.front: How do the steps differ for newcomers by origin?
cards.back: United States and Canadian newcomers surrender and test lightly, other-country newcomers test fully, young visitors obey both states, and nobody under sixteen drives at all.

recaps.module: Who needs a license and license classes

recap_hooks.text: Nobody under sixteen drives; Class D starts at eighteen, or seventeen with driver education, DJ at sixteen, and E adds paid passengers.
Size or service makes a license commercial.

recaps.module: Enhanced, REAL ID and the R endorsement

recap_hooks.text: The Enhanced license crosses borders; REAL ID meets federal checkpoint standards, and both work for domestic flights.
The R endorsement starts past a weight or length limit, with a road test and no written test.
File form MV-forty-four, then prove your name with six points, one of them signed.

recaps.module: Vision, written test and the permit

recap_hooks.text: Pass the online pre-test, take the receipt to an office, and earn the permit with vision, the written test and fees.
Junior permits may not drive at night in the city or on Long Island; upstate nights need a listed supervisor.

recaps.module: Preparing for and taking the road test

recap_hooks.text: Practice fifty hours with fifteen after sunset; the point-and-insurance course never replaces the safe-driving course.
Junior licenses carry one non-family young passenger at most, and night rules differ in the city, on Long Island and upstate.
Report an address change within ten days, and newcomers trade in licenses within thirty days.
